title: status/report --run and ACTIVE are not validated: path traversal writes status.md outside the runs dir
detail: resolveRun joins any --run value or ACTIVE contents onto the runs dir and only checks existence; renderStatusFile then overwrites <that dir>/status.md. `status --run ../../..` overwrote a user's status.md; `--run ''` renders the runs dir; a tampered ACTIVE does the same via report.
fix_hint: Validate RUN_ID for the flag and the ACTIVE value in resolveRun and check the resolved dir stays under runsDir; exit 1 otherwise. Tests for --run '../x', --run '' and a tampered ACTIVE.

title: An existing local path containing whitespace is classified as paste
detail: The whitespace→paste check runs before the existence check, so a real directory like '/Users/x/My Tool' becomes type=paste with identity sha256 of the path string, marked fetched, next=inventory.
fix_hint: Check exists(path.resolve(text)) for single-line text before the whitespace heuristic. Add a classifySource test with a directory name containing a space.

title: A non-existent path or schemeless URL is silently treated as a one-word paste
detail: './missing/dir' or 'github.com/foo/bar' fall through to paste; the run is created with fetched=true and ACTIVE moves to it. The user never gets an error.
fix_hint: Paste positional text only when it contains whitespace or a newline; refuse a single path-like or host-like token that does not exist or has no scheme, with a hint to use --as paste or a full URL.

title: A value flag given with no value silently falls back to the default
detail: parseArgs stores true for a bare flag and consumers ignore non-strings: `status --run` renders ACTIVE, `intake src --run` auto-names, bare --as/--slug/--project are dropped, `--paste-file` with no value reads stdin. Unknown flags are accepted.
fix_hint: Declare value flags (run, project, as, slug, paste-file) and fail with usage when one has no string value; reject unknown flags per verb.

title: Manifest identity skips symlinks, so distinct sources collide
detail: Dirent.isFile() is false for symlinks, so a directory holding only a symlink and an empty directory both hash to sha256 of '\n'; lookupSource would then report reuse_from for an unrelated source.
fix_hint: Include symlinks in the manifest as entries (path\t->target) and make an empty manifest an error or salt it. Test a directory containing a symlink.

title: --paste-file silently discards a positional source
detail: With --paste-file set, classifySource returns paste and the positional URL or path is ignored without an error.
fix_hint: Fail with usage when --paste-file is combined with a positional other than '-'. Add a CLI test.

title: Status shows fetch as done for local/paste even though fetch never ran
detail: The spec says fetch for local/paste records a zero-egress row; nextStep instead returns inventory right after intake and the table marks fetch done with no egress row.
fix_hint: Have intake record the zero-egress row itself for local/paste so the done state is true, or derive fetch completion from an egress row. Update tests.

title: Any non-undefined decision counts as decided
detail: nextStep treats null, '' or 'maybe' as decided while summary counts the same power as undecided.
fix_hint: One shared predicate: decided means one of rebuild|use|buy|skip.

title: --paste-file is decoded as UTF-8 before hashing
detail: Invalid UTF-8 bytes become U+FFFD so the identity and paste.txt no longer match the file's real bytes.
fix_hint: Read the paste file as a Buffer; hash and write raw bytes; decode only for the emptiness check.

title: A non-object .claude/bbs.json crashes with an opaque TypeError
detail: bbs.json of null, [] or a scalar makes deepMerge return that value; every verb dies with 'Cannot read properties of null'.
fix_hint: Require a plain object after JSON.parse and throw `invalid config in <file>: expected an object`.

title: Run id date is UTC, not the local date
detail: West of UTC an evening intake gets tomorrow's date, disagreeing with marathon run ids and the user's calendar.
fix_hint: Use the local date, keeping the injected now() for tests.

title: Concurrent intakes can pick the same run id and overwrite each other's run
detail: runIdFor checks existence but the run dir is only created later inside writeJson; nothing claims the id in between. 6 parallel intakes with the same slug: 3 got the same runId, one source.json survived, egress.jsonl collected 4 rows.
fix_hint: Claim the id atomically: fs.mkdir(runDir) without recursive; on EEXIST move to the next -n suffix (for --run, fail). Only then write source.json. Test parallel intakes get distinct ids.

title: source.json is written before the paste and egress row, so an interrupted intake leaves a run that looks complete
detail: source.json (fetched:true) is written first; paste.txt is a plain non-atomic write; a later failure leaves a run that nextStep reports as inventory while paste.txt may be missing or truncated and no longer matches the identity.
fix_hint: Write fetched/paste.txt atomically and the egress row first; write source.json last as the commit marker, or remove the run dir on any failure after the claim.

title: A local git repo with no commits cannot be taken in
detail: isGitRepo only checks .git exists; `git rev-parse HEAD` fails on an unborn HEAD or a missing git binary, intake aborts and git's stderr is printed raw and repeated.
fix_hint: Catch the git failure and fall back to the path+size manifest (or fail with a clear message); use stdio ['ignore','pipe','pipe'] in defaultGit.

title: A literal null row in egress.jsonl crashes status and report
detail: readJsonl keeps any JSON value; a `null` line enters state.egress and the bytes_in reduce dereferences it. lookupSource has the same unguarded access. Corrupt rows are dropped silently.
fix_hint: readJsonl keeps only plain-object rows and counts the rest as corrupt; show the corrupt-row count in status.

title: status.md is written non-atomically and status fails outright on a read-only run dir
detail: renderStatusFile uses a plain writeFile; on EACCES the read-only status verb exits 1 without printing the markdown it already rendered.
fix_hint: Write status.md via the tmp+rename helper; in the status verb print the markdown even when the write fails and warn on stderr.

title: Project root silently falls back to cwd when git is missing or fails
detail: If git is missing, resolveProjectDir uses cwd; from a subdirectory a second .claude/bbs tree is created and later status calls from the root cannot find the run.
fix_hint: Walk up from cwd looking for .git or .claude when git is unavailable, or warn on stderr and point to --project.

title: ACTIVE pointer written non-atomically; a full disk wipes the previous run's pointer
detail: setActiveRun uses fs.writeFile which truncates first; on ENOSPC the old pointer is gone and the rollback cannot restore it (empty reads as null). Every other store write is atomic; this one is not.
fix_hint: setActiveRun via writeTextAtomic(file, runId+'\n'). Test that a failing write leaves the prior ACTIVE intact.

title: Stdin paste is decoded as UTF-8, which corrupts non-UTF-8 bytes and its identity
detail: readStdin decodes to a string so invalid sequences become U+FFFD; different pastes can hash equal and lookupSource reports a false reuse_from; the same bytes via --paste-file get a different identity.
fix_hint: Return a Buffer from readStdin; hash and write raw bytes as --paste-file does; decode only for the emptiness check. Test equal identities for a non-UTF-8 byte via stdin and via --paste-file.

title: Without a git checkout, the marker walk silently roots the project at ~/.claude
detail: Every Claude Code user has ~/.claude, so from any non-git directory under $HOME the walk stops at $HOME with no warning and runs land in ~/.claude/bbs.
fix_hint: Skip os.homedir() when matching the .claude marker (or stop the walk at $HOME, keeping only .git there) so the warn-and-use-cwd fallback applies. Test with HOME set to a temp dir containing .claude.

title: Running cli.js through a symlinked path does nothing and exits 0
detail: The main-module guard compares the realpath of import.meta.url with path.resolve(process.argv[1]) which keeps the symlink; through a symlinked dir every verb is a silent no-op with exit 0.
fix_hint: Compare fs.realpathSync of both sides inside try/catch. Test running the CLI through a symlinked directory.

title: Run ids are case-insensitive, so the same --run means one run on macOS and two on Linux
detail: RUN_ID accepts uppercase and explicit ids are stored as given; APFS merges Foo/foo, Linux does not.
fix_hint: Lowercase explicit run ids or reject uppercase by dropping the /i flag.

title: URL/repo credentials in the source ref are saved in plaintext to source.json, status.md and stdout
detail: storedRef keeps userinfo and the query string as given; a ref like https://alice:ghp_SECRET@host/x?token=abc lands in source.json, the JSON result and status.md, and later in egress.jsonl and the registry.
fix_hint: Refuse refs with userinfo (or strip it) and redact query values whose key looks like token/key/secret/sig/auth in every persisted or printed copy of ref. Test that no ghp_-style string reaches source.json or status.md.

title: git rev-parse HEAD inherits GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE from the environment, so identity can come from a repo the user did not name
detail: defaultGit runs with the full process.env; with GIT_DIR set, git ignores cwd and the run gets another repo's identity, so lookupSource can attach reuse_from to an unrelated run.
fix_hint: Run git with GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES and GIT_CONFIG_* removed from env, or pass explicit --git-dir/--work-tree. Test with GIT_DIR pointing elsewhere.

title: A .git file or symlink in a local source sends rev-parse to a repository outside the named directory
detail: isGitRepo only checks <ref>/.git exists; a gitdir file or symlink pointing elsewhere lets a crafted directory impersonate a known identity.
fix_hint: lstat <ref>/.git: a symlink or a gitdir file resolving outside ref falls back to the manifest identity with an identity_note.

title: Config paths.runs / paths.registry can point writes outside .claude/bbs
detail: runsDir and registryPath join cfg.paths.* with no containment check; paths.runs '../escaped' created run dirs outside the project while ACTIVE stays hardcoded.
fix_hint: In loadConfig, reject paths.runs/paths.registry that are absolute or do not resolve under <project>/.claude/bbs, failing loudly with the key.

title: Stray positional arguments are silently ignored, so `status <run-id>` reports a different run
detail: status and report never read positionals and intake uses only the first; `status first` prints the active run, `report nonsense-run` prints the active run's counts, `intake a.txt extra` drops extra silently.
fix_hint: Reject positionals a verb does not take with the verb's usage plus `unexpected argument "<arg>" (use --run <id>)`; allow at most one positional for intake. Test per verb.

title: Run-id errors name the input but not the fix
detail: invalid run id / unknown run / already exists messages give neither the accepted format nor the next step.
fix_hint: Append the rule and the next step to each message.

title: Usage text hides the per-verb flags and the `-` stdin source
detail: Top-level usage does not name --next, --project, --as, --slug or --paste-file; INTAKE_USAGE never says <source> may be `-` for stdin.
fix_hint: Print each verb's usage line from FLAGS; write <source|-> and note that - reads stdin.

title: `paste is empty` does not say which input was empty
detail: Same message for stdin and --paste-file.
fix_hint: Name the source: paste is empty (stdin) / (--paste-file p).

title: `report` fails outright on a status.md write error, naming a temp file
detail: status warns and continues; report aborts and the error names the random tmp path.
fix_hint: Use renderStatusSafe in report with the same warning line, naming status.md and the run dir.

title: 'omit --run to use the active run' is printed when the id already came from ACTIVE
detail: resolveRun builds the same unknown-run message whether the id came from --run or from ACTIVE; with a stale ACTIVE the advice loops.
fix_hint: Branch on whether --run was given; name ACTIVE and the next step.

title: Empty-paste error says (stdin) when the empty paste was the source argument
detail: content falls back to String(ref) but the label only distinguishes --paste-file from everything else.
fix_hint: Label by origin: --paste-file, stdin, or the source argument.

title: git clone follows HTTP redirects to any host without the per-hop host check
detail: The repo path checks the ref host once; git's http.followRedirects stays at its default so a 30x from the named host can land on 127.0.0.1, 10.x or 169.254.169.254, unchecked and unlogged.
fix_hint: Add -c http.followRedirects=false and -c credential.helper= to the clone args; assert them in the clone-args test.

title: Clone checkout runs global filter drivers (git-lfs) that fetch from repo-chosen hosts
detail: Only GIT_CONFIG* env is scrubbed; ~/.gitconfig still loads, so with git-lfs installed the smudge filter downloads from an lfs.url the cloned repo chooses, bypassing checkHost and the egress log.
fix_hint: GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1, -c filter.lfs.smudge= -c filter.lfs.process= -c filter.lfs.required=false, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 and GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, -c protocol.allow=never with only https/ssh allowed; assert in the clone-args test.

title: url fetch requests the redacted ref, not the URL the owner named
detail: intake masks token-like query values; fetchRun then fetches ?key=%3Credacted%3E, so the page is wrong or 4xx and the identity comes from a URL nobody named.
fix_hint: Refuse in fetchRun when source.ref contains <redacted>, with a message telling the owner to re-run intake with the URL without that value. Test it.

title: --max-links / max_urls is checked once per fetch, not per request, so redirects exceed it
detail: The limit is compared with logged requests before the fetch; fetchUrl can then make up to max_redirects+1 more requests; failed-then-retried fetches add more.
fix_hint: Pass the remaining URL allowance into fetchUrl and refuse with a refused row before any hop that would pass it. Test --max-links 1 with one redirect.

title: Clone egress row reports bytes_in 0; clone has no byte limit and no timeout
detail: The git row always records bytes_in 0; max_bytes and the 30 s timeout never apply to the clone; execFileSync has no timeout so a stalled server or ssh prompt hangs forever.
fix_hint: Measure fetched/repo after clone and log it as bytes_in; refuse and remove when over the remaining allowance; pass timeout to execFileSync; GIT_SSH_COMMAND='ssh -o BatchMode=yes'.

title: Repo clone accepts http:// and git:// although the spec allows only https:// and git@ shapes
detail: hostOfRef is the only scheme gate in cloneRepo, so http:// and git:// refs are cloned over plaintext transports.
fix_hint: In cloneRepo accept only https://, ssh:// and user@host:path; refuse http:// and git:// with a refused egress row and exit 2. hostOfRef may still parse git:// (its test stands).

title: No test shows --max-bytes / --max-links change what fetch does
detail: Only flag validation and usage text are tested; the per-run limit test drives limits through cfg, never through maxBytes/maxUrls or the CLI flags.
fix_hint: Add a fetchRun test with maxBytes/maxUrls overriding a larger cfg limit, and a CLI test where --max-bytes 5 with a pre-seeded egress row refuses with exit 2.

title: Refused rows count as requests in the egress line and the url budget
detail: isRequest counts every http/git row including pre-connect refusals, so requests=1 is reported when nothing was sent and refusals use up max_urls.
fix_hint: Count a row as a request only when it was actually sent (no pre-connect refused, or carries a status/bytes); keep refusals in the refused count.

title: Too-many-redirects refusal writes no refused egress row
detail: The max_redirects refusal throws after logging only the 3xx status row, so the log never shows the run was refused.
fix_hint: Log a refused row for the next hop before throwing, as refuse() does.

title: Redirect and byte limits are not tested at their exact boundary
detail: The loop test checks 10 redirects refused, never that exactly 5 are followed and a 6th refused; size tests use 100 vs 50, never maxBytes vs maxBytes+1.
fix_hint: Assert 6 calls for a 5-redirect chain that succeeds and refusal for 6; an exact-maxBytes body succeeds and maxBytes+1 is refused.

title: A failure after the source.json commit deletes fetched/ while source.json still says fetched
detail: result() runs inside the try after the commit marker; if loadState/readJsonl throws, the catch removes fetched/ and the run is left fetched:true with no files; a retry says already fetched.
fix_hint: Build the result outside the try/catch that removes fetched/, or set a committed flag after writeJson and skip the rm. Test: loadState throws after commit → fetched/ survives.

title: Corrupt egress.jsonl rows are silently dropped from the max_urls/max_bytes accounting
detail: readJsonl without report skips unparsable lines, so used.requests and used.bytes_in undercount and the per-run limits fail open on a corrupt log.
fix_hint: Read with report:true; when corrupt > 0 refuse naming egress.jsonl and the count (or count each corrupt row as a full request). Test with a truncated last row.

title: Host lookup runs outside the request timeout, so a hanging resolver blocks fetch indefinitely
detail: checkHost runs before the AbortController timer on every hop and in cloneRepo; a lookup that never settles hangs the verb.
fix_hint: Race the lookup against timeoutMs with an EgressRefused('cannot resolve <host>: timeout after N ms'). Test with a lookup that never resolves.

title: A failed or timed-out clone logs bytes_in 0 although data was transferred
detail: On git error or timeout the partial dest is removed and the row records only error with bytes_in 0, so repeated failed attempts read unaccounted bytes.
fix_hint: Measure treeBytes(dest) before the rm and log it as bytes_in on the error row.

title: An empty or absent response body is committed as a successful fetch
detail: A 2xx with a null or zero-byte body writes an empty file and marks fetched:true with the sha of the empty string, so every empty-body source shares one identity.
fix_hint: Treat a zero-byte 2xx body (and 204) as a fetch error leaving source.json unfetched. Test 204 and empty 200.

title: GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null is ignored on git < 2.32, so ~/.gitconfig still applies to the clone
detail: Git reads GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL only from 2.32; older gits (Debian 10, Ubuntu 20.04, RHEL 8) still load ~/.gitconfig, so url.insteadOf can rewrite the clone URL past checkHost, http.extraHeader/cookieFile can send auth, and other filter drivers can run.
fix_hint: In cloneEnv also set HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME to an empty temp dir; assert them in the clone-env test.

title: Clone -c settings persist in fetched/repo/.git/config, including core.hooksPath pointing at a deleted temp dir
detail: Options after `clone` are written into the new repo's config; core.hooksPath keeps pointing at a deleted /tmp dir another local user could recreate and plant hooks in.
fix_hint: Use core.hooksPath=/dev/null (no temp dir), or pass settings as top-level `git -c` options so nothing persists.

title: Real network failures surface only undici's generic 'fetch failed' and the cause is dropped
detail: Node's fetch rejects with TypeError('fetch failed') and the real reason in err.cause; the error and the egress row log only err.message.
fix_hint: Build the text from err.cause (code or message, recursing into AggregateError.errors) for both the egress row and the thrown Error; test with a fake fetchImpl throwing TypeError('fetch failed', {cause}).

title: Fenced JSON fails for ```json with CRLF, ```JSON, or a trailing space after the fence tag
detail: Only an exact '```json\n' prefix is stripped; other variants leave the tag in place, and the bare-fence branch cuts at the first ``` anywhere, so a value containing ``` breaks valid input.
fix_hint: Match the fence with a regex tolerant of case, trailing spaces and CRLF, and take the closing fence from the end of the text. Test CRLF, ```JSON and a value containing ```.

title: The 'in our words' check rejects short prose ideas and accepts real code
detail: Lines starting with this/for/new/type/return/default count as code, case-sensitively, even for a one-line idea; Python and a fenced block after a prose line are accepted.
fix_hint: Reject any ``` fence anywhere; count code lines only when the idea has 3+ lines; use language-neutral signals (trailing ; { or def/fn patterns, leading indentation). Test a one-line lowercase prose idea (accepted) and code after prose (refused).

title: Power name accepts newlines, markdown pipes, path segments and __proto__
detail: Names are only trimmed and capped; 'a|b\n# x', '../../etc/passwd' and '__proto__' were accepted; later steps key on the name (map --from, briefs/<power>.md, tables).
fix_hint: Restrict names to one line of letters, digits, space, dot, underscore, dash; refuse / \\ | control chars, a leading dot, and __proto__/constructor/prototype; report the index. Test each.

title: Licence detection takes the first match in walk order and misses LICENSE-MIT / LICENSE-APACHE
detail: A nested licence can win over the root one depending on readdir order, and the pattern misses LICENSE-MIT.
fix_hint: Gather all candidates, prefer the shallowest path then alphabetical; widen the pattern to /^(LICEN[CS]E|COPYING)([.-]|$)/i. Test root vs nested and LICENSE-MIT only.

title: listSourceFiles returns an empty list when the root cannot be read
detail: readdir errors are swallowed; a moved or deleted local dir yields a brief with zero files and 'use unknown'. New instance of 'fail loudly'.
fix_hint: stat the root first and throw naming the path; re-throw or record subdirectory errors. Test a local source removed after intake.

title: The no-overwrite check on powers.json is a check-then-write gap
detail: fs.stat then writeJson; two concurrent runs without --force can both write and the last silently wins. New instance of 'claim atomically'.
fix_hint: Without force, claim exclusively: write tmp then fs.link(tmp, powersFile) (EEXIST) and unlink tmp, or open with 'wx'. Keep tmp+rename for --force.

title: --force keeps the old map.json, verdicts.json and handoff.json, which were built for the replaced powers
detail: After a forced re-inventory, nextStep finds old judgments/decisions under reused names and can report later steps done for powers never re-judged.
fix_hint: Under --force, move map.json/verdicts.json/handoff.json aside as *.stale-<ts>.json and say so in the result. Test: inventory, write map.json, inventory --force, next is map.

title: A truncated brief tells the helper to 'ask for a narrower slice', but nothing provides one
detail: No flag selects a slice, so a helper following the text replies in prose, which the JSON-only contract forbids.
fix_hint: Replace with an actionable line (inventory only the listed files; name unlisted top-level dirs in evidence) or add --path <prefix> to --brief and name it.

title: The brief lists .env and key files and tells the helper to read every listed file
detail: Only .git and node_modules are skipped; .env, .npmrc, id_rsa, *.pem are listed under 'read the source files', so secret values can land in evidence/idea and powers.json.
fix_hint: Omit secret-like names (.env*, *.pem, *.key, id_*, .npmrc, .netrc, credentials*) from the list, show a count of omitted files, and tell the helper never to copy values from config or secret files. Test that .env is absent.

title: Duplicate names are not compared after Unicode normalisation or whitespace collapsing
detail: NFC vs NFD and double spaces are accepted as different powers.
fix_hint: Compare on normalize('NFC').toLowerCase() with whitespace collapsed; store the NFC form.

title: A non-string or untrimmed none_found is stored as given
detail: none_found: 5 or true is accepted with a powers list; '  x  ' is stored untrimmed.
fix_hint: Refuse a present non-string none_found; store it trimmed.

title: The 500-file cap is applied after a full walk, and the kept files are the first 500 in walk order, not sorted
detail: The whole tree is walked synchronously regardless of maxFiles and the kept slice depends on filesystem order.
fix_hint: Collect paths, sort, then slice; use async fs.lstat.

title: No test covers skipping symlinks or a repo-type source in listSourceFiles
detail: No symlink (including one pointing outside the root) and no repo-type run with fetched/repo/.git are tested.
fix_hint: Add a symlink to ../outside and assert it is absent; add a repo-type run and assert the listed paths.

title: A failure after powers.json is committed fails the verb, and a retry is refused with 'powers.json exists'
detail: loadState/nextStep after the link run outside any try and throw on a corrupt map.json or EACCES on egress.jsonl; the new powers.json stays and the next plain --from says pass --force. Same commit-then-fail pattern as fetch r2.
fix_hint: Once the link or rename succeeds the write is done: wrap the re-render and loadState/nextStep in try/catch, return next:null plus a warning naming the unreadable file, exit 0. Test with a corrupt map.json and no powers.json.

title: The exclusive claim needs hard links; on filesystems without them every non-force inventory fails with a raw EPERM/ENOTSUP
detail: Only EEXIST is translated; EPERM/ENOTSUP/EXDEV from fs.link are rethrown raw so inventory can never succeed without --force on exFAT/SMB/FUSE.
fix_hint: On EPERM/ENOTSUP/ENOSYS/EXDEV fall back to fs.open(powersFile,'wx') + write + fsync. Test with an injected link that throws EPERM.

title: A --force that fails partway leaves files moved aside with no rollback and no report
detail: A rename or the final write can fail after earlier renames; the error does not list what was moved; a same-ts stale name is overwritten silently.
fix_hint: On failure after the first rename, rename moved files back or include stale_moved in the error; claim the stale name with wx/link or a random suffix.

title: An empty or vanished source root still produces a normal-looking brief with no files
detail: An empty fetched/ passes the stat check and the brief prints 'Read the source files above' with an empty list.
fix_hint: When total is 0 throw 'source root <root> has no files — re-run fetch/intake'. Test with an empty fetched/.

title: The walk visits the whole tree one lstat at a time, even after maxFiles is reached
detail: Only .git and node_modules are skipped; .venv, target, dist, vendor are walked in full with one awaited lstat per entry.
fix_hint: Use Dirent types to skip lstat where possible, batch per directory with Promise.all, and skip common build/vendor dirs.

title: The 'JSON only' parse error does not say which input it came from and echoes raw bytes
detail: The same message for --from <file> and stdin; binary stdin prints control bytes.
fix_hint: Pass a label (path or stdin) into parseInventory and escape control characters in the preview via JSON.stringify.

title: Non-UTF-8 file names are reported as missing (ENOENT) and dropped from the listing and the count
detail: readdir with utf8 replaces invalid bytes with U+FFFD so the joined path no longer names the real file; such files land under Could not read as ENOENT and are left out of total.
fix_hint: Read directories with encoding 'buffer' and lstat/recurse with Buffer paths; display names with escaped bytes or list them as EILSEQ errors. Test with a fake readdir.

title: SKIP_DIRS is applied to files too, so a file named build, dist, target or vendor is silently left out
detail: The name check runs before the type check; match is exact-case.
fix_hint: Apply SKIP_DIRS only to directories after the type is known. Test a file named build at the root.

title: On NFS a link() that succeeded but whose reply was lost returns EEXIST and is reported as 'powers.json exists'
detail: Any EEXIST from link is treated as someone else's file although our own call created it; the tmp is removed so nlink cannot tell.
fix_hint: On EEXIST from link, lstat tmp first: nlink 2 means the link succeeded — treat as committed; only report EXISTS when nlink is 1.

title: The hard-link path commits powers.json without fsync, while the fallback path fsyncs
detail: writeFile(tmp) then link never syncs; after a crash powers.json can exist zero-length.
fix_hint: Write tmp through a FileHandle and sync() before link, matching the fallback.

title: Empty-input error does not name the input, unlike the parse error fixed in r1
detail: 'JSON only — got empty input' ignores the label.
fix_hint: Use `JSON only — <label> is empty`; CLI tests for --from - with empty stdin and an empty --from file.

title: Power names in scripts that need combining marks are rejected even after NFC
detail: NAME_RE allows only \p{L} and \p{N}; Devanagari, Thai and Arabic names keep \p{M} marks after NFC and are refused.
fix_hint: Allow \p{M} after the first character. Test a Devanagari name.

title: Power name tokens weigh 9×, not 3×: tripled in the token list and then given a ×3 boost
detail: matchPower adds tokenize(name) three times AND passes boost 3 for name tokens, so the name weighs 9× and body occurrences of name tokens are tripled too; on this repo's harness the stored top-5 differs from the spec formula for 4 of 4 sample powers.
fix_hint: Weight the name 3× in one place only (single copy with boost 3). Pin a numeric score against the formula with a name-only vs body-only candidate pair at a 3:1 ratio.

title: A bare-string judgment of 'have' or 'partial' is recorded with tool null and skips the candidate check
detail: The string form sets tool null and bypasses the tool and candidate checks; a 'have' nobody can check makes defaultVerdict skip. The contract test at line 214 enshrines a bare 'partial'.
fix_hint: Accept the bare string only for missing; refuse bare have/partial with a message naming {status, tool, why}. Change the line-214 test to the object form and add a test that a bare have is refused.

title: Fenced JSON with a trailing newline, CRLF or leading whitespace is rejected as 'JSON only'
detail: Fences are stripped only by a strict prefix/suffix; a file ending in ```\n or a CRLF fence fails. Inventory r1 fixed this exact pattern.
fix_hint: Share inventory's fence/JSON parser (export it) and reuse it. Tests for trailing newline, CRLF and ```JSON.

title: map --force drops judgments but leaves verdicts.json and handoff.json built on them
detail: After re-judging, nextStep finds old decisions and moves to handoff or done; inventory has STALE_ON_FORCE, map has no equivalent; recordJudgments --force has the same gap.
fix_hint: Under --force move verdicts.json and handoff.json aside as *.stale-<ts>.json (share inventory's helper) and report stale_moved. Test: map, judge, write verdicts.json, map --force, judge → next verdict.

title: Tests miss input shapes the contract names, and the name-×3 test passes with the boost deleted
detail: The ×3 test uses what:'x' idea:'y' which tokenize to nothing, so the ranking is the same at 1×, 3× or 9×; untested: --from <file>, fenced/CRLF judgments, map --force CLI, bare have, symlinks under index roots, --force with --brief.
fix_hint: A test where name and body compete with a pinned score; CLI cases for --from <file>, a fenced file with trailing newline, map --force after judgments, a symlinked command file.

title: The map --from parse error does not name its input and echoes raw control bytes
detail: Same message for stdin and file; raw CR/LF printed.
fix_hint: Pass a label from the CLI and JSON.stringify the preview (shared parser).

title: The brief says 'Only these 5 candidates' even when a power has fewer or none
detail: matchPower returns [] for no shared tokens; the brief still says 5 and does not say missing is the only valid answer.
fix_hint: Print the real count; when 0 print 'no candidates — answer missing'.

title: Index globs are wider than the spec: nested skills, nested hooks, nested plugins and any *SKILL.md
detail: Skills, hooks and plugins are walked recursively; endsWith('SKILL.md') matches MYSKILL.md.
fix_hint: Limit depth per kind: skills exactly .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md, hooks and plugins depth 1.

title: Unparseable package.json and symlinked index entries are dropped silently
detail: A JSON.parse failure is swallowed; Dirent symlinks are skipped with no record.
fix_hint: errors.push({path:'package.json', code:'EJSON'}); record skipped symlinks with code SYMLINK.

title: The index walk reads whole files for 80 lines and ignores the 'Walk only what you will use' rule
detail: Files are read fully then sliced; the walk awaits one entry at a time; only node_modules/.git skipped; no cap.
fix_hint: Read a bounded 64 KiB prefix via FileHandle; skip SKIP_DIRS; batch per directory; cap rows per kind.

title: Dead code: an unused ts and empty writeError branches
detail: const ts never used; renderStatusSafe writeError checked and ignored in empty if blocks.
fix_hint: Remove the unused ts; return the warning in the result or drop the redundant calls.

title: A failure after map.json is committed fails the verb (buildMap and recordJudgments)
detail: renderStatusSafe calls loadState outside its try; a corrupt verdicts.json/handoff.json or EACCES on egress.jsonl throws after map.json is written; a retry of recordJudgments is refused with already judged. Same commit-then-fail pattern fixed in writeInventory.
fix_hint: After the map.json write, wrap renderStatusSafe in try/catch in both functions and the CLI finally; return a warning naming the unreadable file, exit 0. Test with a corrupt verdicts.json.

title: A corrupt map.json cannot be rebuilt even with --force
detail: readJson(mapPath) runs before the force check and throws on corrupt JSON.
fix_hint: With --force, catch the corrupt-JSON error, count 0 judgments dropped, move the corrupt map.json aside; without --force keep the error and say --force will rebuild. Test with a truncated map.json.

title: Check-then-write gap: a concurrent map and map --from can silently drop judgments or overwrite a rebuilt map
detail: buildMap checks judgments, builds the index slowly, then overwrites map.json; recordJudgments reads, validates, writes back. Either can lose the other's write.
fix_hint: Compare-and-swap on map.json ts just before the final write, or hold an exclusive map.lock ('wx') around the read-modify-write in both functions.

title: Status is rendered twice and a write failure is reported twice
detail: The library renders and returns a warning; the CLI finally renders again and warns on stderr.
fix_hint: Render in the finally only on the error path, or drop it from the library.

title: The per-kind cap records the limit, not how many files were left out
detail: capped.command is 2000 with nothing saying how many were dropped; the kept rows are not the lexicographically first.
fix_hint: Keep counting after the cap and record capped[kind] = {kept, total}.

title: A power named "judgments" is mistaken for the wrapper object
detail: parsed?.judgments ?? parsed treats any top-level judgments key as the wrapper.
fix_hint: Unwrap only when judgments is the sole key, a plain object, and not a power name.

title: A slow map run can lose map.lock to a second process, and the first run's finally then deletes the second run's lock
detail: The lock mtime is never refreshed while buildIndex runs under it; a second process sees it stale, removes it and takes its own; the first run's finally rm's without checking ownership. Breaking a stale lock also races, and NFS clock skew can make a fresh lock look stale.
fix_hint: Build the index before taking the lock; write a random token + pid into map.lock and remove it only if the token is ours; break a stale lock by rename then token check; refresh mtime every 20 s while fn runs. Test with an injected now where fn outlasts the stale window.

title: tokenize splits on combining marks and does not normalize, so Devanagari/Thai names are lost and NFD text never matches NFC powers
detail: [^\p{L}\p{N}] treats \p{M} as a separator; no NFC normalisation.
fix_hint: Normalize NFC before lowercasing and split on [^\p{L}\p{M}\p{N}]+. Tests for a Devanagari name and an NFD row vs NFC power.

title: package.json is read whole and its scripts bypass the per-kind cap; a UTF-8 BOM drops every script as EJSON
detail: Unbounded readFile; scripts rows pushed after capList; JSON.parse rejects a leading BOM.
fix_hint: Strip a leading BOM; put package.json scripts through the cap accounting; stat first and refuse over a size limit with a named error.

title: A failing lock release after map.json is committed fails the verb
detail: fs.rm force ignores only ENOENT; EACCES/EBUSY/EIO throw after the map.json write.
fix_hint: Wrap the release in try/catch; after fn resolved, a release failure becomes a warning naming map.lock.

title: Symlinked index roots (.claude, .claude/hooks, scripts, src/lib, package.json) are followed out of the project without a SYMLINK report
detail: listFiles skips symlinked entries inside a directory but the roots and their parents are never checked; symlinked scripts/, .claude/hooks and package.json pointing outside were read (first 64 KiB) and indexed as if inside, with errors [].
fix_hint: lstat each root and each parent up to projectDir; a symlink → errors {path, code:'SYMLINK'} and skip; same for package.json; or realpath each root and refuse those not under realpath(projectDir). Tests for a symlinked scripts/, .claude and package.json.

title: licenceClass strips parentheses, so a grouped OR beside an AND is classed permissive
detail: '(MIT OR Apache-2.0) AND Proprietary', '(MIT OR GPL-3.0) AND BUSL-1.1' and 'GPL-3.0 AND (MIT OR Apache-2.0)' all return permissive; they should be commercial, commercial, copyleft. legalVerdicts then lets use through for a licence with a binding proprietary or copyleft term.
fix_hint: Parse SPDX with precedence (AND tighter than OR, parentheses group); strictest-of-AND, most-permissive-of-OR over the tree; unbalanced or unrecognised → none. Tests for the three cases and nested groups.

title: BBS_SANDBOX=present in any shell replaces real sandbox detection in the shipped CLI
detail: A leftover export or a CI env marks the sandbox present without running docker info; a permissive power with a clean probe then gets use on a machine with no sandbox, with no stderr trace.
fix_hint: Honour only absent (the safe direction) with a stderr warning naming BBS_SANDBOX; refuse present with exit 1.

title: Config sandbox.required_for_use:false makes use legal with no sandbox
detail: A .claude/bbs.json override silently removes a rule the spec says cannot change; no warning, no reason recorded.
fix_hint: Always require a present sandbox for use; ignore false with a stderr warning naming .claude/bbs.json.

title: Several input shapes and switches the contract names have no test of their own
detail: Untested: CLI --from <file>/--from -/missing file; BBS_SANDBOX=present and invalid; --evidence alone; --table after a probe changed legality; a refused --decide leaving verdicts.json and labels.jsonl byte-identical; grouped licence expressions; probe --force clean→found clearing a use decision.
fix_hint: Add each as its own case.

title: Probe evidence is stored and printed verbatim, with no length cap and no redaction
detail: Evidence for a found probe often quotes the URL found, which can carry a token.
fix_hint: Cap at 2 KiB, strip control characters, redact with intake's redactRef-style helper before storing or printing.

title: A decision cleared after the registry row and labels were written leaves them claiming the cleared verdict
detail: probe --force found/incomplete or a recompute after the sandbox disappears nulls the decision in verdicts.json only; registry.jsonl latest row still says use and labels.jsonl keeps label 1.
fix_hint: When a decision with a label/registry row behind it is cleared, append a superseding registry row and a withdrawal label row. Test: decide all, re-probe found --force, lookupSource no longer returns use.

title: If the registry or labels append fails after commit, there is no clean way to retry
detail: A failed appendRegistry/labels append is only a warning; resubmitting is refused with already decided; --force duplicates labels and appends another registry row; the warning names no repair command.
fix_hint: Make the repair idempotent: resubmitted identical decisions skip the refusal and append only missing label/registry rows; name the repair command in the warning. Tests for each append throwing then a retry.

title: inventory --force does not take map.lock, so a running probe or decision can write a stale verdicts.json back
detail: writeInventory --force moves verdicts.json aside without the lock; a concurrent recordDecisions writes the old rows back beside the new powers.json.
fix_hint: writeInventory --force takes withMapLockDetailed around the stale move and the powers.json write; or store powers.json ts/identity in verdicts.json and refuse a mismatched write.

title: Wrong advice and counts when verdicts.json is corrupt or unreadable
detail: The --force hint is appended to every read failure including EACCES; --force overwrites a corrupt file instead of moving it aside; dropped reports 0 although unknown.
fix_hint: Hint only for corrupt JSON; move the corrupt file aside; report dropped as unknown.

title: docker stderr goes into the stored and printed reason with no length cap or control-character stripping
detail: firstLine(docker.stderr) is stored verbatim in sandbox.reason and repeated in rows and the table; stdout is piped and never read.
fix_hint: Strip control chars and cap at ~200 chars; spawn with stdio ignore/ignore/pipe.

title: The unshare failure reason does not say why
detail: ENOENT, EPERM and timeout all collapse to unshare is unavailable.
fix_hint: Build the reason from code/status/first stderr line like dockerWhy.

title: A power listed twice in the decisions input is silently resolved to the last value
detail: JSON.parse keeps the last duplicate key with no warning.
fix_hint: Detect duplicate top-level keys and refuse naming the power.

title: On a filesystem without hard links, breaking a stale map.lock can silently steal another process's fresh lock, so two holders run at once
detail: When the stale-break content check fails, the lock is put back with fs.link; on exFAT/SMB/FUSE link throws and the catch swallows it and continues, so B's open('wx') succeeds while A still holds the lock.
fix_hint: Restore with fs.rename after checking the path is free (or link falling back to rename); if the restore fails, throw held() naming the aside file — do not retry. Test with an injected link that throws EPERM.

title: docker info against a remote daemon (DOCKER_HOST / docker context) counts as a sandbox on this machine and makes use legal
detail: With DOCKER_HOST=tcp:// or ssh://, or a remote docker context, docker info exits 0 and the sandbox is recorded present although this machine has none; ssh:// can also prompt on /dev/tty.
fix_hint: Count docker only when the endpoint is local (unix:// or npipe; DOCKER_HOST unset or unix://), using docker context inspect or docker info --format; otherwise present:false with 'docker daemon is remote (<redacted endpoint>) — not a sandbox on this machine'. Tests with DOCKER_HOST=tcp:// and ssh://.

title: Sanitised sandbox stderr and probe evidence keep Unicode bidi and line-separator characters, and the 200-char cut can split a surrogate pair
detail: CONTROL_CHARS strips only C0/C1; bidi overrides and U+2028/2029 pass through; slice cuts by UTF-16 unit.
fix_hint: Strip \p{Cf}-style format chars (keep \n) and cut by code point. Tests for U+202E and an emoji at the boundary.

title: recordDecisions and recordProbe trust row.legal and vj.sandbox stored in verdicts.json, so use can be decided from a stale file
detail: use is checked only against stored needs_probe/legal; neither the current licence policy nor a fresh sandbox check is consulted; a verdicts.json computed while docker ran (or by an earlier build counting a remote context) lets --probe clean + --decide use succeed with no sandbox.
fix_hint: Inside the lock re-derive each named row via recomputeRow against the current power + cfg licence class; before accepting use require vj.sandbox.present true, probe clean AND a fresh detectSandbox present. Test: stale verdicts.json with sandbox present, sandbox now absent → refused exit 2.

title: A WITH exception is ignored, so Apache-2.0 WITH Commons-Clause or MIT WITH GPL-3.0 classify as permissive and make use legal
detail: atom() skips the exception id; restrictive exceptions unlock use for a non-permissive licence.
fix_hint: Classify the exception: an allowlist of permission-granting SPDX exceptions (LLVM-exception, Classpath-exception-2.0, GCC-exception-*, Autoconf-exception-*, Bison-exception-*, Font-exception-2.0, OpenJDK-assembly-exception-1.0, Universal-FOSS-exception-1.0) keeps the base class; anything else → the stricter of base and none (or the exception's own class). Tests for Commons-Clause → not permissive, LLVM-exception → permissive.

title: Any failed docker context inspect (timeout, non-zero exit) is treated as a local endpoint, so docker info may then reach a remote daemon
detail: dockerEndpoint maps every non-ok inspect to local and detectSandbox then runs docker info with the same env; a podman shim with CONTAINER_HOST=ssh:// or a timeout fails open.
fix_hint: A failed inspect counts as local only when stderr shows the context command is unknown; ETIMEDOUT or any other non-zero → present:false naming the inspect failure, no docker info. Tests for inspect timeout and non-zero status.

title: The docker/unshare stderr kept in sandbox.reason is not redacted and carries private paths into verdicts.json, status.md and labels.jsonl
detail: 'Cannot connect to the Docker daemon at unix:///Users/<user>/.docker/run/docker.sock' is stored and repeated everywhere including withdrawal reasons.
fix_hint: Run the line through redactUrlsInText, replace os.homedir() with ~, pass scheme URLs through redactDockerEndpoint. Test with a home-path stderr.

title: The verdict table does not show needs_probe: an unprobed power lists use as legal and gives no reason
detail: verdictTable has no probe column and Why holds only removed reasons; an unprobed permissive power with a sandbox shows use as legal with no caveat, and the owner's pick is then refused with exit 2. needs_probe appears only in the JSON.
fix_hint: When needs_probe is true, mark the Legal cell 'use (probe first)' and add 'use needs a clean network probe (cli.js verdict --probe <power>=…)' to Why; show the probe result when present. Add a verdictTable test with a needs_probe row.

title: PolicyRefused messages leave out the cause and the next command
detail:
' is not legal for

: legal verdicts are …' omits the removed reason and gives no next command; the needs_probe refusal names the command but not the legal set.
fix_hint: Append the matching removed reason and 'choose one of them with cli.js verdict --decide <power>=<verdict>'; add the legal set to the needs_probe refusal.

title: A refused buy (and the table's missing buy) names no cause: legalVerdicts only records a removal reason for use
detail: --decide x=buy on a permissive power is refused without a cause; Why never says why buy is absent.
fix_hint: Push {verdict:'buy', reason:'licence <cls> — buy is legal only for a commercial licence or a power that sends data off the machine'} when buy is not legal; test a refused buy quotes it.

title: Module header says use is never legal without a clean probe, but legalVerdicts lists use before any probe
detail: legal includes use with needs_probe true before the probe; what is enforced is that a use DECISION needs a clean probe.
fix_hint: Reword the header: use is never a default; a use decision is accepted only with a permissive licence, a sandbox on this machine and a clean probe (listed as needs_probe before).

title: sanitizeStderr docstring says only non-http schemes are cut to scheme+host, but http(s) URLs are cut too
detail: SCHEME_TOKEN also matches the already-redacted http(s) URL and drops its path and query.
fix_hint: Fix the docstring to say every scheme token except unix:// and npipe:// is cut to scheme + host[:port].

title: With a powers.json that has no ts, the guard says powers.json changed and its advice loops
detail: powers_ts null vs undefined throws POWERS_CHANGED with a false cause; re-running verdict writes null again.
fix_hint: Refuse in computeVerdicts when powers.json has no ts with a ts-specific message, or compare (vj.powers_ts ?? null) === (powers.ts ?? null).

title: Repair hint always says --from <same file>, even when the input came from --decide or stdin
detail: After --decide the warning names a file that does not exist.
fix_hint: Build the hint from the input label: re-run cli.js verdict <label> to append the missing rows (stdin: resubmit the same input on --from -).

title: handoff proceeds when some powers have no decision; undecided powers silently vanish
detail: Only verdicts.rows being an object is checked; an undecided power is in neither powers nor skipped, handoff.json is written and next=done. No powers_ts check either.
fix_hint: Refuse unless every power in powers.json has a decided row and powers_ts matches; name the undecided powers and the --decide command. Test with one decided and one not.

title: marathon slug is only the last dash segment of the run id, so different sources share one marathon run
detail: initSlug uses run.split('-').pop(); '2026-10-07-claude-suite' → bbs-suite; same-day init reuses the run dir and the second handoff overwrites the first source's finish line and adds streams to it.
fix_hint: Slug = the run id minus its date prefix; refuse when init returns a run that already has non-default lines or streams. Test two sources sharing a last segment.

title: queued streams' plan path briefs/<slug>.md does not resolve from the marathon run or project root
detail: The brief lives under .claude/bbs/runs/<run>/briefs/; the stream row stores a bare relative path and kickoff.md names neither the bbs run nor the brief dir, so a resume session cannot find the brief.
fix_hint: Store a project-relative path; name the bbs run and brief paths in kickoff.md; assert path.join(dir, rows[0].plan) exists.

title: a failure after marathon init leaves an ACTIVE half-filled run that the error does not name
detail: init succeeds, stream fails: the marathon run dir stays with ACTIVE pointing at it and finish-line/kickoff overwritten; the error does not name it.
fix_hint: Catch after init and name the run and the recovery in the error (re-run --force or remove it); test a runner that succeeds at init and fails on stream.

title: two buy powers that slug alike overwrite each other's memo
detail: The slug collision check covers only rebuild/use; 'X Y' and 'x-y' both write memos/x-y.md.
fix_hint: Check slug collisions across every approved power before writing anything.

title: per-power line filter uses endsWith('_'+slug), so one power picks up another's checks
detail: Powers 'b' and 'a_b': tests_green_a_b ends with _b, so b's brief lists a_b's checks.
fix_hint: Return lines per power from buildFinishLine or match exact ids base_slug.

title: evidence stripping keeps code that comes before the first —, newline, backtick, ( or {
detail: 'return a+b; src/x.js:3' lands in the brief verbatim; the spec says a brief never includes source code; the line is appended unlabelled.
fix_hint: Extract only location tokens (path:line, URL) with a positive pattern; put them under a labelled Provenance bullet. Test code before the location.

title: marathon run dir is hardcoded and the runId returned by init is used without validation
detail: Files go to path.join(projectDir, '.claude/marathon', runId) ignoring init's runDir and the marathon paths.runs; a runner returning ../../evil wrote outside .claude/marathon.
fix_hint: Use initData.runDir resolved under projectDir, validate runId, assert it sits under the marathon runs dir, pass --run <id> to stream calls.

title: a corrupt finish-line.example.json silently falls back to the default tolerance
detail: A bare catch swallows the parse error; a malformed tolerance error does not name the file.
fix_hint: Fall back only when absent; rethrow parse errors; prefix tolerance errors with the file path.

title: kickoff.md is overwritten wholesale, dropping init's title, Budget and Models sections
detail: The seeded kickoff with Budget and Models is replaced; decide/ask sections left as '- '.
fix_hint: Fill the Done means and Never sections in place and keep the rest.

title: buy memo location differs from the spec, and the memo is thin
detail: Spec says briefs/, code uses memos/; Why buy repeats the idea; no provenance beyond data_needed.
fix_hint: Align the spec with memos/; add source ref, run and network to the memo.

title: Failures after init has moved ACTIVE but before the guarded block do not say so, and a corrupt finish-line.json also blocks --force
detail: Non-JSON init output, a checkInit refusal or a corrupt finish-line.json/streams.json read throw a bare error while ACTIVE points at the new run; under --force a corrupt old finish-line.json is read before force is checked, so the suggested recovery fails every time.
fix_hint: Put everything after a successful init inside the same recovery wrapper (or restore prevActive before rethrowing); under force treat an unparseable old finish-line.json/streams.json as 'holds' and overwrite. Tests for non-JSON init output and a corrupt finish-line.json.

title: --force refill leaves stale queued stream rows (and briefs) for powers that are no longer rebuild/use
detail: Rows are only upserted for current powers; a power now skip/buy keeps its queued row pointing at an old brief; with zero approved powers on refill the old marathon run is never touched while handoff.json says marathonRun null.
fix_hint: On a forced refill mark every stream row not in the new set blocked with a reason (the marathon CLI has no remove verb), delete stale briefs/memos, and when approved is empty name/clear the previously recorded marathon run. Test: first hand-off two rebuild powers, forced one has one.

title: A tolerance the marathon gate accepts (null = unlimited) is refused with a wrong message
detail: validateTolerance allows null for high/medium/low; buildFinishLine insists on numbers and tells the user to change a valid config.
fix_hint: Accept null or a non-negative integer for high/medium/low; require only passes_in_a_row. Test with a null limit in the example file.

title: Check-then-write on handoff.json with no lock: concurrent handoff, or handoff during verdict --from, can produce a stale or interleaved hand-off
detail: The stat and the final write are separated by every brief write and the marathon calls; handoff reads verdicts.json without the lock recordDecisions holds.
fix_hint: Run buildHandoff inside withMapLockDetailed (the run lock verdict uses) and re-check verdicts/powers_ts inside it; claim handoff.json exclusively at the end.

title: From a linked git worktree, init and stream calls hit the main checkout's marathon dir while handoff writes into the worktree's
detail: The bridge runs the marathon CLI with cwd=projectDir and no --project; the CLI maps a linked worktree to the main checkout, so init creates the run there while handoff writes finish-line.json into the worktree's .claude/marathon and fails on a missing kickoff.md; the --force hint fails the same way.
fix_hint: Pass --project <projectDir> on every marathonRunner call. Test from a git worktree add checkout.

title: Synchronous execFileSync under the run lock stops the lock refresh, so a slow init or many stream calls make map.lock look stale
detail: execFileSync blocks the event loop so the 20 s refresh cannot fire; N stream calls back to back can exceed the 60 s stale window and a concurrent command takes the lock mid-write.
fix_hint: Run the marathon CLI with promisified execFile (async) so the refresh keeps running, or touch the lock between calls; keep per-call timeouts well below the stale window.

title: A failed or timed-out init leaves ACTIVE moved to a half-made run without restoring it or saying so
detail: marathon init sets ACTIVE before printing JSON; a non-zero exit or a timeout after that throws a bare marathon: <line> without restoreActive or naming the run.
fix_hint: In the init catch await restoreActive() and append the 'ACTIVE was restored' text; name the run dir init may have created.

title: The claimJson fallback without hard links can leave an empty or partial handoff.json
detail: The wx fallback writes directly; a write failure leaves a truncated file that reads as done and refuses later runs.
fix_hint: On a write failure in the fallback branch remove the file this call created before rethrowing.

title: When an older helper's init output is rejected, the error does not name the run dir it left behind
detail: checkInit refuses and restores ACTIVE but the seeded run dir stays undiscovered.
fix_hint: Name the likely run dir (or the raw output's runDir/id) and say it may need removing.

title: Evidence URLs and dotted tokens are copied unredacted into briefs and memos
detail: evidenceLocations keeps any http(s) URL verbatim and its path.ext pattern matches JWT-shaped tokens; the text is written into briefs and memos.
fix_hint: Pass URL matches through redactRef (or redactUrlsInText first); keep a bare dotted token only with a '/' or a ':line' suffix and drop long base64-like segments. Test a userinfo URL, an ?api_key= URL and a JWT-shaped string.

title: Forced-refill cleanup deletes every .md in briefs/ and memos/, not only the files a hand-off created
detail: A user-written briefs/notes.md or a hand-edited brief is deleted silently; a directory named x.md makes fs.rm throw after the marathon run was filled and before handoff.json is written.
fix_hint: Remove only files listed in the previous handoff.json that are not kept now; skip non-regular entries. Test that a foreign .md survives --force.

title: marathon_cli path is executed without a containment check
detail: paths.marathon_cli '../../elsewhere/cli.js' passes config validation and node runs code outside the project.
fix_hint: Refuse a marathon_cli that resolves outside the project, with the same error shape as the paths.runs check.
